 Actor Anthony Ippolito, 27, spent months training in a boxing gym while learning Sylvester Stallone's specific dialect
 By
 Tracy Wright Fox News 
 Published
 November 20, 2026 9:00am EST Comments

 close Video 'I Play Rocky' star Anthony Ippolito transforms into Sylvester Stallone 
 Anthony Ippolito told Fox News Digital that he endured an "entire lifestyle" change to portray Sylvester Stallone in "I Play Rocky."
 NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!
 Anthony Ippolito's transformation into Sylvester Stallone for "I Play Rocky" didn't happen overnight.
 Ippolito, 27, packed on the pounds and overhauled his diet to portray the heavyweight boxer in the Peter Farrelly-directed biopic about the making of the Academy Award-winning film, "Rocky."
 The New York native explained how he endured "an entire lifestyle shift" before jumping in front of the camera to film "I Play Rocky," which follows Stallone's pursuit to bring Rocky Balboa to life on the big screen — a movie Stallone not only wrote in a few days as a struggling actor, but also refused to sell to a major studio unless he played the starring role.
 JOHN MADDEN ROLE PUSHES NICOLAS CAGE TO DRAMATIC PHYSICAL TRANSFORMATION WITH ‘BRUTAL’ DIET, PROSTHETICS 
 AnnaSophia Robb starred as Sylvester Stallone's first wife, Sasha Czack. (Claire Folger/ 2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.) 
 "I had to gain a bunch of weight," Ippolito told Fox News Digital of his incredible transformation to play the boxer, which included the main priority of "eating a ton of food" every day before focusing on his actual diet and training.
 WATCH HERE: ‘I PLAY ROCKY' STAR ANTHONY IPPOLITO TRANSFORMS INTO SYLVESTER STALLONE 
 Video "So, because knowing Stallone was playing Rocky, who is a heavyweight boxer in the movie, and he was a huge fan of Steve Reeves growing up," Ippolito explained of his preparation for becoming Rocky Balboa.
 SYLVESTER STALLONE CALLS HIMSELF AN 'IDIOT' FOR DOING HIS OWN STUNTS, DETAILS NINE BACK SURGERIES 
 Reeves was known for enduring multiple full-body workouts per week to not only create, but also maintain his fighting physique, and prior to starring in the '58 Italian classic "Hercules," Reeves was credited with bringing bodybuilding to a global level as Mr. America in 1947, followed by Mr. Universe in 1950.
 Sylvester Stallone wrote "Rocky" and starred as boxer Rocky Balboa. (Getty Images) 
 Anthony Ippolito trained for months to become Sylvester Stallone in "I Play Rocky." (Claire Folger/2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.) 
 Ippolito gained more than 30 pounds and spent months weightlifting and training in a boxing gym while also learning Stallone's specific dialect to transform into Rocky Balboa.
 "Stallone started weightlifting at a really young age, so he always had some type of physique," Ippolito said.
 Advertisement
 "It's something that's a really recognizable part of 'Rocky,' and I kind of knew I had to be there, so it was an entire lifestyle shift, to be honest with you."
 SYLVESTER STALLONE'S ADVICE TO THOSE WHO ARE STRUGGLING 50 YEARS AFTER 'ROCKY' CHANGED HIS LIFE 
 Ippolito's transformation completely astounded the Academy Award winner, who admitted that he had "mixed" feelings about the film but was ultimately blown away by his character.
 Anthony Ippolito stars as Sylvester Stallone in "I Play Rocky." (Claire Folger/2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.) 
 Sylvester Stallone filmed "Rocky" by the Schuylkill River in Fairmount Park, Philadelphia, with the old Pennsylvania Railroad Bridge in the background. (Silver Screen Collection) 
 While promoting his memoir, "The Steps," earlier this year, The Hollywood Reporter noted how Stallone grappled with the idea of the biopic and was initially "kind of mixed because I'm going, 'I’m not dead yet. Aren’t we jumping the gun a little bit?'"
 "And then I saw this video of this kid [Ippolito]. I actually thought it was me the first moment; there were a couple of angles. I go to my daughter and say, 'That’s unbelievable.'"
 PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE 
 Ippolito was equally blown away by the compliment from the "Rocky" mastermind, and admitted "it's really, really unbelievable, very surreal."
 "And it means so much, because obviously, especially throughout making this, I only became a bigger fan of his in terms of what he was able to persevere through," Ippolito said.
 Written by Peter Gamble and directed by Peter Farrelly, "I Play Rocky" followed Sylvester Stallone's quest to bring Rocky Balboa to the big screen. (Claire Folger/2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.) 
 "It's just, it's kind of incredible. And so hearing him say that is really, really, really cool."
 GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE 
 "I Play Rocky" follows Stallone's quest to not only write a marketable film for a movie studio, but also his own pursuit in refusing to sell his words unless he was the actor reciting the script.
 After a back-and-forth with producers and ultimately denying himself a massive payout to sell the film prior to its creation, Stallone banked on himself to create the '76 flick with a $1 million budget.
 Behind-the-scenes production comes to life in Peter Farrelly's "I Play Rocky," where crews piece together a big-idea movie with relatively low funds and arguably over-the-top dreams. The director explained how Balboa's laser-focused Hollywood pursuit in the '70s wasn't too far off from the Tinseltown of today.
 LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS 
 Stephan James starred as Carl Weathers in "I Play Rocky." (Claire Folger/2026 Amazon Content Services LLC.) 
 Sylvester Stallone and Carl Weathers on set of the film "Rocky" in 1976. (United Artists/Getty Images) 
 "I do believe that you could create your own 'Rocky' thing," Farrelly told Fox News Digital. "But the key is, it's like what Matt Damon and Ben Affleck did with 'Good Will Hunting.' They wrote that script, and they wanted to get rid of them. They said, no, we're in it. And ... if they hadn't, we probably wouldn't know who those guys are today.
 "But the key to doing something like this is you have to have that script. The script's the most important thing. Script is your ticket. If you don't have a script, you get no power."

 He added, "And I tell people, I say, 'You wanna get in and write a script. That's what Wes Anderson did, you know, with Owen Wilson, Luke Wilson. They wrote their own thing, 'Bottle Rocket,' ... Some people can't write, and you gotta get lucky, but if you can write, you gotta weigh in."
